message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.1","text":"I, Clement, am a Roman citizen, and I have been able to live my earliest years with self-control, because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied with dejection and distress. For a thought about death was continually with me—I do not know where it began—repeatedly reminding me that when I die, I do not exist, and no one will ever make mention of me, since infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion. I shall be nonexistent, aware of no beings, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, not coming into being. And has the world ever come into being, and before it came into being, what then existed? For if it always existed, it will also exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what in turn will exist, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν εἴς τε ἀθυμίας καὶ πόνους","chosen":"because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied with dejection and distress","rationale":"Construes the genitive absolute causally and preserves the image of thought occupying or diverting Clement’s desire."},{"source_quote":"πυκνὰς ποιούμενος ὑπομνήσεις","chosen":"repeatedly reminding me","rationale":"The phrase depicts the thought as continually producing reminders."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος","chosen":"since infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion","rationale":"Preserves the personification of time and the emphatic πάντων τὰ πάντα."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς","chosen":"aware of no beings","rationale":"This compact rendering reflects the surrounding catalogue of nonexistence while leaving the phrase’s uncertain internal scope to the source issue."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τάχα ἔσται τι ὃ νῦν νοῆσαι οὐ δυνατόν","chosen":"And perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived","rationale":"νοῆσαι denotes mental conception or apprehension."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς","issue":"The construction has no expressed accusative referent for ὄντας and permits materially different construals: οὐκ may yield the contextual sense “aware of no beings,” while a more directly substantival reading of οὐκ ὄντας would be “knowing those who do not exist.” The supplied wording is retained without emendation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"1.2","text":"Constantly pondering these and things like them—I do not know from where—I experienced such painful grief that, having grown pale, I wasted away. And most terrible of all, if I ever resolved to push the concern away as useless, the affliction became still more intense for me. I was distressed at this, not knowing that I had a noble thought as a housemate, one that would become for me the cause of a good immortality, as I later learned by experience and thanked God, the Master of all. For by the thought that distressed me at first, I was compelled to come to the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I counted as wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of counting blessed.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὀδυνηρὰν εἶχον λύπην τοσοῦτον ὡς ὠχριακότα με τήκεσθαι","chosen":"I experienced such painful grief that, having grown pale, I wasted away","rationale":"Preserves both the physical pallor and the image of wasting or melting away under grief."},{"source_quote":"ἀκμαιότερόν μοι μᾶλλον τὸ πάθος ἐγίνετο","chosen":"the affliction became still more intense for me","rationale":"ἀκμαιότερον describes the condition as becoming stronger or more acute."},{"source_quote":"σύνοικον καλὴν ἔχων ἔννοιαν","chosen":"I had a noble thought as a housemate","rationale":"Retains the domestic image of the thought dwelling with Clement; καλὴν characterizes it as good or noble."},{"source_quote":"ἀθανασίας ἀγαθῆς αἰτίαν μοι γενησομένην","chosen":"one that would become for me the cause of a good immortality","rationale":"Keeps the explicit qualification ἀγαθῆς, which may distinguish a beneficial immortality from an enduring condition of punishment."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὴν τῶν πραγμάτων ζήτησιν καὶ εὕρεσιν","chosen":"to the investigation and discovery of realities","rationale":"Preserves the paired movement from inquiry to discovery; πραγμάτων here concerns the realities or matters under investigation."},{"source_quote":"ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον","chosen":"I counted as wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of counting blessed","rationale":"Preserves the deliberate opposition between declaring people wretched and declaring them blessed."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.3","text":"From childhood onward, then, while absorbed in such reasonings, I used to attend the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing else there except dismantlings and constructions of doctrines, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time, to give an example, the view that the soul is immortal prevailed; at another, the view that it is mortal. So whenever an argument that it was immortal prevailed, I rejoiced; but whenever one that it was mortal prevailed, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I could not establish either of the two as certain in my own mind. Nevertheless, I perceived that judgments about the theses are regarded as false or true according to those who defend them and do not appear as they actually stand with respect to truth. Having therefore at last taken note that a firm grasp does not arise from the theses being defended, but that judgments are pronounced according to those defending them, and now reeling still more amid these matters, I consequently groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither capable of establishing anything as certain, nor could I shake off concern for such matters, although I wanted to, as I said before. For when I ordered myself more and more often to be still, I do not know how, the thought about such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς","chosen":"I used to attend the philosophers’ schools","rationale":"The imperfect indicates habitual attendance, while διατριβαί denotes places or circles of philosophical instruction."},{"source_quote":"δογμάτων ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς","chosen":"dismantlings and constructions of doctrines","rationale":"Preserves the paired destructive and constructive operations performed on philosophical doctrines."},{"source_quote":"συλλογισμῶν τέχνας καὶ λημμάτων ἐπινοίας","chosen":"techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises","rationale":"λήμματα are propositions or premises adopted for argument, while τέχναι emphasizes methodical techniques."},{"source_quote":"φέρε λέγειν","chosen":"to give an example","rationale":"The parenthetical expression introduces an illustrative case."},{"source_quote":"οὐδ᾽ ὁπότερον εἰς τὸν ἐμὸν βεβαιῶσαι νοῦν ἠδυνάμην","chosen":"I could not establish either of the two as certain in my own mind","rationale":"ὁπότερον refers to the two competing alternatives concerning the soul’s mortality."},{"source_quote":"οὐ παρὰ τὰς ἐκδικουμένας ὑποθέσεις ἡ κατάληψις γίνεται","chosen":"a firm grasp does not arise from the theses being defended","rationale":"κατάληψις is philosophical apprehension or secure cognitive grasp, not merely receipt of information."},{"source_quote":"λανθανόντως μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς ὁ τῶν τοιούτων μοι εἰσήρχετο λογισμός","chosen":"the thought about such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure","rationale":"Keeps both the stealth conveyed by λανθανόντως and the expressly pleasurable quality conveyed by μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἔτι μᾶλλον ἰλιγγίων ἐν τοῖς πράγμασιν. διὸ ἐκ τοῦ τῆς ψυχῆς βάθους ἐστέναζον","issue":"The printed period separates the nominative participle ἰλιγγίων from the following finite verb ἐστέναζον. The translation construes the participial phrase circumstantially with that following verb while retaining the causal force of διὸ; this is an interpretation of the supplied editorial punctuation, not a proposed change to the Greek wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.4","text":"Again, being at a loss, I said to myself, “Why am I laboring in vain? The matter is clear: if, when dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. Therefore I will reserve grieving for that time, when, not existing, I will not grieve. But if, after all, I am something, then grieving now is superfluous for me.” Immediately after this, another thought entered me, for I said, “What if, indeed, because I have not lived devoutly, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, and according to the accounts of certain philosophers I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and shall be in Hades, punished for all time?” Then again I countered, saying, “But these things do not exist.” And again I said, “But what if they do?” Since, then, the matter is uncertain, I said, “It is safer for me rather to live devoutly. And how shall I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the pleasures of the body? But I am not even fully assured what right thing is pleasing to God; nor do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal; nor do I know what reliable argument can be found; nor can I rest from such reasonings.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε","chosen":"I will reserve grieving for that time","rationale":"The feminine article and adverb form an elliptical temporal expression; the translation supplies “time” without treating it as present Greek wording."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα εἰμί τι","chosen":"But if, after all, I am something","rationale":"Retains the deliberately indefinite τι and the inferential or corrective force of ἄρα."},{"source_quote":"νῦν ἐκ περισσοῦ μοι πρόσεστιν τὸ λυπεῖσθαι","chosen":"then grieving now is superfluous for me","rationale":"ἐκ περισσοῦ describes the present grief as excessive or unnecessary."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω","chosen":"What if, indeed, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now","rationale":"Renders the exceptional or apprehensive possibility introduced by εἰ μήτι γε as a natural English self-question."},{"source_quote":"Πυριφλεγέθοντι καὶ Ταρτάρῳ","chosen":"to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus","rationale":"Transliterates the named mythological places rather than replacing them with generalized descriptions."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ᾅδου τὸν αἰῶνα κολαζόμενος","chosen":"in Hades, punished for all time","rationale":"The accusative τὸν αἰῶνα expresses the duration of the punishment."},{"source_quote":"ἀκινδυνότερόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον εὐσεβῶς βιῶσαί με","chosen":"It is safer for me rather to live devoutly","rationale":"Preserves both the comparative safety and the corrective preference expressed by μᾶλλον."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δικαίου χάριν εἰς ἄδηλον ἐλπίδα ἀφορῶν","chosen":"for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope","rationale":"The substantivized adjective refers to what is right, while ἀφορῶν depicts fixing one’s attention on the hope."},{"source_quote":"τίς λόγος βέβαιος εὑρίσκεται","chosen":"what reliable argument can be found","rationale":"In this philosophical context λόγος can denote an argument or reasoned account, and βέβαιος marks it as dependable."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
